title: Generate, run, self-correct: CSV parser vs. a quoted-comma field
taskPrompt: Write a Node.js script named convert.js in the current directory. It reads a CSV file path from process.argv[2], parses it (the first line is the header row, comma-separated), and prints the resulting array of objects as JSON to stdout via console.log(JSON.stringify(...)) — one JSON array, nothing else printed. There is a file check.mjs already in this directory (do not modify it) that verifies your solution — run `node check.mjs` and make sure it prints "CHECK: PASS" before calling finish. If it fails, read the error output and fix convert.js.
